## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bojjhaṅgakathā* (Ps 2.3) is the third treatise of the second major section (*Yuganaddhavagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, translated as the "Discussion of Awakening Factors". Along with related doctrinal expositions in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*—such as the *Indriyakathā* and *Maggakathā*—the text treats its core subject matter through systematic scholastic analyses, examining the nature, purpose, and application (*attha*) of the awakening factors (*bojjhaṅga*) within early Buddhist soteriology [Gethin 2001].

 Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms widespread textual overlap across the Pali canon, detecting 969 matching passages across 42 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest canonical partner is the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46) with 177 matches, followed by internal links to other chapters of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (such as Ps 1.1 *Ñāṇakathā*, Ps 1.3 *Ānāpānassatikathā*, Ps 1.4 *Indriyakathā*, and Ps 2.5 *Virāgakathā*) and the Abhidhamma's *Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 10) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial reuse is also found across the commentarial literature, primarily the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* and the commentaries to the *Aṅguttara*, *Majjhima*, and *Saṁyutta* Nikāyas [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments identified by DharmaNexus include matches with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) as well as Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna texts such as the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* and *Prajñāpāramitā* sutras [DharmaNexus].
